blocks.x: How was living on a boat?

One of the most wonderful things in the first getting experience. You had your tree meals a day. It's up to you if you didn't eat them. You had to miss them. That might be for her. Yeah, you know, they come out every day, and I don't have to ask them for something. I mean, I got too many friends on the boat, so I haven't moved to the public, man. I don't know if you guys would tell me, say whatever.
I was asking you how it was living on a boat.

Yeah, well, I said about three meals a day, and how you could get your clothes clean, or wash them, and do your own washing as a warmer. And at a certain time, you'd have to get new songs on, you'd have to rehearse, but we had the private, the magician had the best break on the job. Nobody would work on the evening, the captain on the down. But that was when anybody worked on the boat, it's when you get up in the morning until time to go to sleep. Everybody had something to do. And they would pick up black and whites, like guys, poor or waiters, deckhands and things like that. Someone would get, you know, get mad, or somebody would have to fire to get in trouble. And we stayed on the top deck, where all the, in other words, we considered this office, where we eat, which was considered like office. The white and the black, helpers or workers on that, they had to have them separated, but they had to set another table. The captain and his, like the ladies that worked, you see, they had a lot of little machines and things on there, operating the machines and things, root beer, things like that. They had about two white, three white ladies, and they had a colored lady and a colored gentleman. They'd been waiting for them a long time. But we'd sleep on the top. In other words, you were just like an official or something. But the other part of the white and the black, some slept on the dance floor and the deckhands slept down in the hall. Now, one black guy, they were waiting for them for a long time. He was dressed up as lightning, the captain, had a uniform and everything. But you see, sometime that boat would have to land somewhere, and it wasn't the proper place. I'd see them land, they'd find this guy out there with a little bit of rope, he'd swim. And he'd get to that tree or railroad track, and I'd say, how the hell did they put that thing on a railroad track? It's dangerous, you know? But they knew what they were doing. And he'd get that little rope, and then he'd put that big rope in. And they'd send the railroad back, and it'd be a difficult place to land, you see. You had to have a man like that. A lot of times, something would go wrong. They'd have to stop in some place and have something done. They had one place. They had a, oh, it was like a big tank, I would say. I can't think of the town. All ships that run on the river could go there and dock up and get a quick repair or a long repair. But we'd always try to get a quick repair, because the captain wouldn't let his boat go that bad, that far, you see. I can't think of that place. We played that city. And it had the river block off like a, you know, this is a bit like a big tank. Must have been about two blocks, three blocks wide, or about eight, six, eight blocks long. And at that time Uncle Sam was building locks on the river, so they'd hold the water back. And that's how they started putting these excursion boats on us. Try like my truck, you try with one, you went with two, and you went with three. Because once in a while we'd get stuck on a sandbar. And that meant you had to play there until they'd get off that sandbar. You'd get stuck on a sandbar in the moonlight. You got to stay there until they'd get off that sandbar.
